findings.area: Scoped IO obligation lifecycle: effect class, scope and liveness
findings.statement: All 16 IO kinds get the same lifecycle and failure rule (reader-io-catalog.json ioKinds[*].failure; model.World.register/failure/unresolved/eligible). That includes read-only observations with no Node-side effect. The model has four problems. (a) A routine read-only failure becomes UNCERTAIN, and only b_settle_uncertain_io (OP + independent physical proof) clears it. (b) Any PENDING_IO in a Node scope denies all 13 readers and refuses signing for that Node. This makes the Node single-flight for every plain and B admission. (c) A fuse-persistence failure on one operation fences the single global completion incarnation, so other Nodes' healthy operations also need OP after a restart. (d) An exact claimed TERMINAL_FRAME continuation is registered through fresh R03 eligibility (zero denial facts). Under DRAIN the 72028 behaviour (terminal.py:78 accepts online|draining) and catalog R12 both allow it, but the model refuses it. Root required no operator intervention for ordinary success, observation/restoration that stays possible, that a wrong-scope obligation never blocks another Node, and no permanent hidden block. Root's registration mandate named node_transport.py:289, build_execution.py:787 and the :835 parented read.

counterexamples.A1 heartbeat timeout: register HEARTBEAT_OBSERVE (/v1/heartbeats, 72028 observation.py:119 via NodeTLSClient.probe), invoke, failure() (a 3 s transport timeout) gives UNCERTAIN. eligible() is false for 13/13 readers. The next successful heartbeat confirms its own obligation, but the Node stays denied. Only an OP settle with a physical-proof record restores it.
counterexamples.A1b in-flight: a registered, in-flight heartbeat with no failure already makes eligible('R03') false for the whole Node.
counterexamples.A2 renewal: after a heartbeat timeout, same-config APPROVAL renewal signing is refused (protected_signing_read: unresolved(s)). The Node can drift to expiry while it waits for OP.
counterexamples.A10 signing starvation: prepare an ARM, then a heartbeat registration on the same Node bumps authorityVersion, then HSM, then publish returns None. Routine observation traffic discards every concurrently prepared signature.
counterexamples.A3 single flight: a second independent EXECUTE registration on the same Node, with disjoint resources, is refused while the first is PENDING. The plain profile is affected too, because readers and procedures are shared. This is an undeclared plain behaviour change from 72028's concurrent leases.
counterexamples.A5 cross-Node fence: register on node-1 and node-2, then failure(node-1, persist_fuse=False) sets the global completionAuthority to FENCED_UNKNOWN. node-2's valid ACTIVE outcome is refused. After restart_verifier, node-2's LIVE capability becomes LOST_INCARNATION, eligible(node-2) is false and only OP can settle it.
counterexamples.A4 terminal under drain: with a DRAIN fact, register(TERMINAL_FRAME) returns None. model.invoke has a DRAIN allowance for TERMINAL_FRAME that can never be reached.
counterexamples.also: buildkit_transport.py:855 (the pre-dispatch quarantine-channel probe) is a read-only IO that this rule would make OP-recoverable. A transient B_GATE_INVALIDATE send failure leaves an UNCERTAIN obligation that needs OP even after a later verified INVALIDATED ACK/readback.

rootDecisionNeeded.question: How should non-side-effect and idempotent-safety IO uncertainty close?

alternatives.A (reviewer recommended): Add a closed per-kind effectClass to ioBinding and the catalog. SIDE_EFFECT (EXECUTE, BUILD_DISPATCH, TERMINAL_FRAME, B_GATE_ARM) keeps Root's UNCERTAIN -> SETTLED_PROTECTED. IDEMPOTENT_SAFETY (CANCEL, QUARANTINE_RECONCILE, B_GATE_INVALIDATE) may close ordinarily only through an independently verified exact command-hash ACK or durable receipt/readback; otherwise protected. READ_ONLY (RECEIPT_OBSERVE, HEARTBEAT_OBSERVE, GPU_ACTIVE_OBSERVE, STORAGE_SAMPLE, OBJECT_READ, BUILD_HEALTH_READ, BUILD_CLEANUP_READ, B_ROLE_OBSERVE, B_FOLDER_ROOT_OBSERVE) failure goes to an ordinary terminal NO_EFFECT_ABANDONED by the verifier, never counts as UNRESOLVED and never bumps the authority anchor version; liveness keeps the existing heartbeat/offline rules.
alternatives.B: Register obligations only at Root's named side-effect sites (:289 execute/cancel, :787, the parented :835, B gate ARM/INVALIDATE). Read-only observation keeps the existing authenticated nonce rules with no obligation.
alternatives.C (not recommended): Keep the uniform OP settle and accept operator escalation for routine read-only loss.

requiredFix: Choose (Root) and encode the effect-class rule in the schema, catalog, authority predicates and model.

Scope the completion fence: a poison/persistence failure fences only that (tenant, Node, epoch, operation) capability. A whole-incarnation fence is reserved for actual verifier process/incarnation loss, and other scopes' LIVE capabilities stay usable.

Decide PENDING_IO admission scope (Root): either it denies only admissions that overlap its run/claim/resource binding (UNCERTAIN SIDE_EFFECT still denies the Node), or Node-wide single flight is declared as an explicit plain behaviour change with its capacity effect.

Register continuation kinds (TERMINAL_FRAME, OBJECT_READ, BUILD_CLEANUP_READ) against the exact claimed operation or parent handle with a per-kind denial-fact policy (DRAIN allowed for the exact claimed terminal), not fresh R03 eligibility.

Stateful fixtures: heartbeat timeout followed by a good heartbeat restores without OP; in-flight read-only does not deny; read-only registration does not discard a prepared signature; a side-effect timeout still requires protected recovery; a node-1 fuse failure does not affect node-2; terminal frame under DRAIN.

findings.area: Typed call classification fails open; 'zero unjustified blockers' is not real feasibility
findings.statement: In source_semantics.enhance, any call that is not a DB record, resolved target, typed transaction owner, typed Mapping/stdlib, or an authority-typed receiver falls into NONAUTHORITY_UNRESOLVED_EXTERNAL_BACKLOG. That bucket carries no provenance and is excluded from both plan closure and plan blockers. It holds 29,573 of the 47,608 call sites. Root required NONAUTHORITY only with actual receiver/source/import/type provenance, resolved Database/BoundDatabase/Session and injected transaction owners, explicit scoped UNKNOWN for dynamic dispatch, and no exclusion of needed call sites. The 21 critical plans are 'SUPPORTED_STATIC_PLAN, 0 unknown' because unresolved edges are dropped, not because they were resolved. The reverse also happens: value-object constructors are BLOCKed.

counterexamples.actual 72028 dropped authority edge: shard_recovery.py:179 `runs, approvals, prepared = RunStore(bound), ApprovalStore(bound), []` and :186 `runs.transition(...)` (the validated->planned run-state writer) are classified as backlog. ShardRecovery.prepare is SUPPORTED_STATIC_PLAN with no RunStore in transitiveFunctions. Synthetic C1 (tuple unpack) is backlog while control C1b (single assignment) resolves to RunStore.transition/_transition.
counterexamples.critical outer transactions unrecorded: `self.db.transaction` at observation.py:52 (NodeObservation.accept), :139 (mark_offline), results.py:164 (ResultStore.complete) and shard_completion.py:46 (ShardCompletion.once) is backlog, not RESOLVED_TRANSACTION_OWNER. 107 transaction/begin calls stay backlog (76 self.db.transaction, 4 runtime(state).transaction, 5 env.db.transaction, ...). The owner fixture M2-runtime-constructor-transaction-owner passes only because its synthetic runtime() returns a literal Database(...); the 4 real runtime(state).transaction sites remain unresolved.
counterexamples.dynamic dispatch: C4 `{"a": leases.lock_run}[k](conn, r, p)` is backlog (not BLOCK). C7 untyped injected `store._admit_locked(conn, p, r)` is backlog.
counterexamples.unjustified BLOCKs: 9 of the 28 BLOCK edges are frozen dataclass value-object constructors reached through a module alias (CapabilityInput, ObservationInput, ContributionInput, Announcement x2, ShardRequirement x2, ArtifactPin, DrillMeasurement) and 3 are Session.in_transaction status reads. They make the plain API entries api.v1.nodes.post_heartbeat, enroll_node and api.v1.storage.register_contribution UNSUPPORTED, with only the generic reason 'unresolved invocation on a source-proven authority receiver' and no scope/binding/future work.

requiredFix: Make the default for an unresolved receiver UNRESOLVED and attach it causally to the affected plans. NONAUTHORITY needs positive provenance: value-object/dataclass with no DB or method calls, stdlib, typed Mapping, external client with a proven non-DB type.

Resolve tuple/starred assignments, constructor-injected attributes (self.db from Database/BoundDatabase at every constructor call site, otherwise an explicit per-plan UNKNOWN_TRANSACTION_OWNER), module-alias class constructors and returned runtime() owners.
Classify dict/list/subscript dispatch of an authority function as a scoped BLOCK.
Give every remaining unknown and SQL issue exact scope/binding/futureWork/blocksGrant fields.

Add actual-source fixtures: ShardRecovery.prepare reaches RunStore._transition; the four critical entries record their outer Database.transaction boundary; dict dispatch gives BLOCK; CapabilityInput gives a non-authority value object; post_heartbeat becomes a usable plan.

findings.area: Semantic writer regression gate misses further shapes
findings.statement: Counterexamples not covered by the 26 owner mutants. C3 `"UPDATE inv.%s SET status='online' ..." % t` and C3b string concatenation of the identifier both record as STATIC_NAMED_SCOPE with no writer and no unknownSqlWriter; the function is not even reached, so the audit is silent. Root explicitly forbade STATIC_NAMED_SCOPE for dynamic identifiers. C5 `session.query(Node).filter(...).update({...})` and C6 `session.bulk_update_mappings(Node, ...)` give a record on public.nodes but no writer. C2 `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(%s), pg_advisory_lock(%s)` is labelled TRANSACTION_ADVISORY (the check is 'xact' in sql) and the plan is SUPPORTED. Semantic from/to checks are hard-coded for about 10 function names; Containment.change, provision/revoke channel enable/expiry and enroll/register have column coverage only. A git grep found no current 72028 instance of C2-C6, so the current 34-writer census is unaffected.
findings.requiredFix: Treat any non-constant SQL composition (BinOp % or +, .format, .join, JoinedStr) reaching execute as DYNAMIC (UNKNOWN/BLOCK) unless it comes from a closed literal set. Detect Query.update/delete and bulk_*_mappings as ORM writers. Classify advisory locks per call occurrence. Add explicit transition semantics for every RULES writer. Add W17-W22 mutants for these shapes.

findings.area: Per-procedure normative lock lists versus the wrapped source body
findings.statement: In 12 of the 39 joined entries in source-procedure-lock-plans.json, the proposed procedure locks table X FOR SHARE while the source body it wraps locks X FOR UPDATE. Examples: PlacementStore.reserve, DeliveryQueue._can_start, ToolGateway.claim, ModelManifestStore._capture, provision/revoke_channel and build_adapter on inv.nodes; RunStore.complete and ResultStore.complete on inv.runs; Containment.change across four procedures. Running the prefix procedure first and then the original body upgrades SHARE to UPDATE inside one transaction, and two concurrent same-Node entries deadlock (PostgreSQL aborts one). 'Strongest mode per row' exists only as prose in plan_specs.withinRankOrder; rank_contract.check validates only rank sorting.
findings.requiredFix: Publish a merged per-entry lock list (procedure plus source plan, strongest mode per row, single acquisition in rank order) and a check that fails on any mode upgrade inside an entry. A two-session PG trace remains required at runtime.
